title: Microsoft Copilot Studio: workflow agent node can return generated files
summary: The planned file output and documented credit controls are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge Microsoft's separately documented workflow billing exception and remove a checklist instruction for a group rule that has no control row.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans Agent node outputs containing generated PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and CSV files.
claims.quote: The Agent node can now return files that the agent generates, such as PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and CSV, as workflow outputs.

claims.claim: The planned file output works with inline agents.
claims.quote: Works with both inline agents and existing (published) agents.

claims.claim: The planned file output works with existing published agents.
claims.quote: Works with both inline agents and existing (published) agents.

claims.claim: Generated files appear as an ordered files output available to downstream steps.
claims.quote: Generated files appear as an ordered files output (name, content type, content) that's available to downstream steps.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the files output as containing name, content type and content.
claims.quote: Generated files appear as an ordered files output (name, content type, content)

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the file output's arrival default or that existing workflows change.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio workflow Agent node generated files output rollout existing workflows default prerequisites. Read the roadmap, agent-node-workflow, flows-overview and FAQ search excerpts; none states a file-output default or migration.

claims.claim: Makers open Workflows in Copilot Studio and can configure an existing published agent or a new inline agent.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, go to Workflows and open an existing workflow, or create a new one. ... An existing agent: Select a published agent from a list. ... New agent for this workflow: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow.

claims.claim: The agent node's Output dropdown controls the shape of the return value.
claims.quote: Use the Output dropdown to control the shape of what the agent returns. The shape determines how downstream workflow steps consume the result.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The cited agent node article does not yet describe the generated files output or its downstream connection identity.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent node files output default disable prerequisites. Read agent-node-workflow in full; Output lists Text response, Structured output and Custom structured output, not the roadmap's files output or its downstream identity.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness natively creates and edits Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files.
claims.quote: It natively creates and edits Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files

claims.claim: The created-files article is preview documentation about files produced during conversations.
claims.quote: Files the agent creates (Microsoft Copilot) (preview) ... An agent can create files during a conversation

claims.claim: Neither the harness overview nor the created-files preview article specifies the Agent node files output design.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio workflow agent node files output; read harnesses-overview and created-files-overview in full. They describe native file capabilities and conversational file cards, not the workflow node's ordered files output.

claims.claim: An agent in a workflow can be grounded in SharePoint knowledge.
claims.quote: SharePoint: Connect to a SharePoint site, library, or specific document so the agent can answer from internal content.

claims.claim: Turning on Work IQ lets the agent use the running user's recent mail, Teams, calendar, OneDrive and SharePoint context.
claims.quote: Turn on Work IQ to let the agent use the running user's recent work activity, including mail, Teams, calendar, OneDrive, and SharePoint context, to ground its responses.

claims.claim: The agent decides at runtime which attached tools to call, their order and their arguments.
claims.quote: The agent decides at run time which of its attached tools to call, in what order, and with what arguments.

claims.claim: The expense-report example includes an approvals action that waits for a reviewer.
claims.quote: Later steps either autoapprove and post the journal entry to the AP system or start an approvals action with the agent's reasoning attached and wait for a finance reviewer.

claims.claim: Evaluations are available only for new agents created in workflows, not existing published agents.
claims.quote: Evaluations are only available for new agents created in workflows.

claims.claim: Running workflows complete normally when new runs are blocked for capacity.
claims.quote: Running workflows complete normally.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, cost; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness workflows use consumption-based billing measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness ... use a usage-based billing structure. ... Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The agent node article warns that using, building, testing and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: The workflows overview says workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action they execute.
claims.quote: Workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action they execute.
claims.fix: After this sentence, add: 'The cost-management page separately lists workflows as covered by a Microsoft 365 Copilot license when run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user, and billed in all other cases.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness, whose workflow table gives this qualification to the overview's general statement.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness experiences charge Copilot Credits for LLM tokens.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness experiences charge Copilot Credits for tools.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness experiences charge Copilot Credits for the harness itself.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs

claims.claim: The environment's prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go plan funds the credit charge.
claims.quote: from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan

claims.claim: The credit charge is not assigned to individual makers or users.
claims.quote: and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A credit rate specifically for generating files in the Agent node has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot file generation credits rate. Read billing-credit-overview and agent-node-workflow; examined requirements-messages-management and AI Builder rate excerpts. None states a rate specific to this workflow files output.

claims.claim: An environment allocation is not a spending boundary if tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go remains available.
claims.quote: An allocation isn't a boundary if the environment can continue drawing from tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant caps prepaid consumption at the environment allocation.
claims.quote: Clear this option to cap prepaid consumption at the environment's allocation.

claims.claim: Disabling tenant prepaid capacity draw does not stop usage through a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: A published environment-group rule governing tenant draw makes the environment setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: An attempted environment override of the published group rule fails with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Administrators can change and republish the group rule or remove the environment from the group to manage the setting independently.
claims.quote: Change and republish the rule for the environment group, or remove the environment from the group to manage the setting independently.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Stop usage turns off an agent when it reaches its monthly credit limit.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Agent monthly limits are not instant and agents may continue responding for some time after reaching them.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts notify administrators but do not stop Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.where: Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Managing capacity requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published prerequisites specific to the Agent node files output.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio workflow Agent node generated files output rollout existing workflows default prerequisites. Opened agent-node-workflow, flows-overview, harnesses-overview and created-files-overview; none gives prerequisites for this node's files output.

claims.claim: The tenant capacity draw setting is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: select Licensing. ... Under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... Select Manage Copilot Credits. ... Select the environment. ... Under Capacity overages, clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 sets the allocation and tenant draw through allocatedEntitlements[].enforcementRules with ruleType TenantPool and enabled false.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"; $apiVersion = "2024-10-01" ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false } ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit opens the monthly limit pane, which also configures the notification threshold.
claims.quote: go to Licensing > Copilot Studio. ... Select Manage Agents. ... Select the agent, and then select Set limit. ... Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit. ... Configure the notification threshold.

claims.claim: An API that sets the individual agent monthly credit limit is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent monthly consumption limit Power Platform API Dataverse bot table Set limit Stop usage. Read manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness, govern-credit-consumption and bot reference (searched credit, monthly, limit, budget); no setting operation found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a UI or API switch specifically turning off file output from the workflow Agent node.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent node files output default disable prerequisites; agent node files disable Dataverse API table. Read agent-node-workflow, harnesses-overview, created-files-overview and bot reference (searched file); no file-output switch found.

claims.claim: Capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio and changes to shared capacity can affect other agents, workflows and features in the environment.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. ... Changes to shared capacity can affect other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in the same environment.

claims.claim: The conversational created-files preview documents a 10 MB per-file limit, without the briefing asserting it applies to workflow output.
claims.quote: Size per created file | 10 MB

claims.claim: The conversational created-files preview documents 28-day retention, without the briefing asserting it applies to workflow output.
claims.quote: Retention (per conversation) | 28 days after the last activity in the conversation

claims.claim: Credit allocations and agent limits govern consumption rather than file formats or downstream file destinations.
claims.quote: Credit allocations and agent limits control consumption. ... An agent-level limit helps contain a single workload, while the environment configuration determines which capacity sources are available to all workloads in the environment.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: Every control that the governance checklist instructs the reader to change appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Where a published environment-group rule governs that setting, change the group rule instead. / The table has environment allocation, agent monthly limit and missing file-output switch rows, but no environment-group rule row.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence 'Where a published environment-group rule governs that setting, change the group rule instead.' from the Before rollout checklist. Keep the existing group-rule qualification and supported remediation in Cost and licensing; do not add a control row.
